subject.title: [Feature]: When building a work system with OpenClaw as the core, WebUI should remain accessible after the Gateway crashes.

question: Should OpenClaw core own a crash-survivor static/rescue WebUI on the Gateway port, or should production availability remain the responsibility of supervised Gateway restarts and external reverse-proxy/service tooling?
rationale: The requested behavior changes Gateway availability architecture and public config/security semantics; source inspection shows no narrow implementation path that avoids a product/security boundary choice.

options.title: Require a rescue-sidecar design first
options.body: Keep this issue open, reject the simple in-process toggle shape, and ask for a Gateway lifecycle/security design before implementation.

options.title: Document supervisor-only recovery
options.body: Decide that launchd/systemd/Windows service recovery and optional reverse proxies are the supported production pattern, then close or convert this to docs work.

options.title: Accept a minimal opt-in static fallback
options.body: Approve a new core config surface and require tests/proof for same-port handoff, auth, origins, TLS, and upgrade behavior before merge.

recommendation.title: Require a rescue-sidecar design first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, reject the simple in-process toggle shape, and ask for a Gateway lifecycle/security design before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled history across Gateway lifecycle, Control UI, and config surfaces affected by this decision.
